title: NEB Class 12 Physics — Ray Optics — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Derive the relation between the focal length and the radius of curvature of a concave mirror, and state the mirror formula.
questions.solution:
For a ray parallel and close to the principal axis striking at height h on a mirror of radius R, the normal is the radius. By the small-angle geometry, the reflected ray crosses the axis at F where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, giving h/R ≈ 2(h/f) for paraxial rays, hence **f = R/2**.

The mirror formula follows from similar triangles for a general object distance u, image distance v: **1/v + 1/u = 1/f** (with the Cartesian sign convention).
questions.knowledgeNote: The result holds only for paraxial rays — spherical aberration is the failure for wide beams.

questions.question: What is total internal reflection? State the conditions for it to occur and one application.
questions.solution:
**Total internal reflection** is the complete return of light into a denser medium when it strikes the boundary with a rarer medium beyond the critical angle.

**Conditions:** (i) light must travel from denser to rarer medium, (ii) the angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle C, where sin C = 1/n.

**Application:** optical fibres (also: totally reflecting prisms in periscopes, brilliance of diamonds).
questions.knowledgeNote: sin C = 1/n gives C = 42° for glass–air and about 49° for water–air — the denser the medium, the smaller the critical angle.

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms a real image 30 cm from the lens. Find the object distance and the magnification.
questions.solution:
1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/30 − 1/u = 1/20 → −1/u = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so u = **−60 cm** (object 60 cm in front).

m = v/u = 30/(−60) = **−0.5** — the image is real, inverted and half the size.
questions.knowledgeNote: Real images have positive v and negative m (inverted); virtual images have negative v and positive m.
